title: Prefill/Decode Attn-Cost Sculptor: dynamic phase split with attention-cost signals
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Current prefill/decode scheduling treats tokens and batches largely uniformly which causes tail latency for requests with high attention compute (long context, dense attention patterns). We need a scheduler that uses an attention-cost signal (attn-cost estimate per request) to sculpt phase splits dynamically so we can preserve P99 latency SLOs while maintaining throughput and fairness across tenants.

Goals: 1) incorporate a lightweight attention-cost estimator into admission and phase-splitting decisions; 2) enable fine-grained phase-splits that keep heavy-attn requests in isolated microbatches or slower lanes to avoid degrading short low-attn latency requests; 3) preserve tenant fairness via credit smoothing rather than hard starvation; 4) keep implementation incremental and reversible behind feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce an attention-cost estimator that runs in <500us per request and correlates >=0.7 with actual kernel time on representative workloads
New phase-split policy reduces P99 latency for low-attn requests by >=15% under mixed workloads (measured on canary infra)
Overall throughput degradation <=5% for mixed workloads compared to baseline when policy enabled
No tenant experiences >25% increase in 95th percentile latency over 7-day canary period without explicit config
Feature gated, rollout documented, and runtime metrics emitted to console: attn_cost_estimate, split_decision, lane_id, tenant_credit_delta
experiments: Microbench: run synthetic mix of short low-attn prompts and long high-attn prompts on dev-gpu-4 to validate estimator correlation
A/B canary on dedicated pool: 5% traffic with policy enabled, compare P50/P95/P99 and token/sec with baseline over 48h
Fairness stress: 50 tenants with skewed traffic profiles to validate credit smoothing prevents starvation over 24h ramp
Kernel-level trace: capture prefill/decode timeline and kernel execution durations for cases where estimator mispredicted >2x
rollout_plan: Feature flag start: runtime.attn_sculptor=false by default
Stage 1: Enable on internal test harness only (dev and perf clusters)
Stage 2: Canary 5% traffic on dedicated pool with close monitoring and rapid rollback playbook
Stage 3: 25% traffic after 72h stable canary, then 100% after 7 days if metrics stable
Emergency rollback: revert flag + restore previous policy, automated alert to SRE and oncall
monitoring: Dashboards: Attn Cost Estimator health, estimator vs kernel_time correlation, split_decision distribution by tenant
Alerts: estimator_correlation < 0.6 for 30m, P99 latency increase >20% over baseline for low-attn requests
Logs: decision events include request_id, tenant_id, attn_cost_estimate, lane_id, credit_balance
SLOs: maintain P99 < configured_target for priority lanes; track change relative to baseline
